sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) Name the product of ethyne with cold alkaline KMnO4 (b) State Markovnikov's rule.
questions.answer: (a) Oxidised to oxalic acid (sodium oxalate), decolourising the purple colour. (b) The negative part of an unsymmetrical reagent adds to the carbon of the double bond with fewer hydrogens.

questions.q: (a) What is the product of ozonolysis of ethene? (b) What is pyrolysis of alkanes?
questions.answer: (a) Two molecules of methanal (HCHO). (b) Decomposition of alkanes on heating to high temperature in the absence of air into lower alkanes and alkenes.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions. (b) Alkenes show addition reactions due to the presence of σ bonds.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – due to the π bond.

questions.q: Fill in: (a) The hybridisation of carbon in ethene is ______. (b) The shape of ethyne is ______.
questions.answer: (a) sp². (b) linear.

questions.q: Match: (a) Wurtz reaction (b) Baeyer's reagent (c) Lindlar's catalyst with (i) partial hydrogenation of alkyne (ii) 2RX + 2Na (iii) cold alkaline KMnO4.
Write (a) the reaction of calcium carbide with water and (b) the general formula of alkynes.
questions.answer: (a) CaC2 + 2H2O → C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. (b) CnH2n−2.

questions.q: Name (a) the product of nitration of benzene and (b) the catalyst for Friedel–Crafts reactions.
questions.answer: (a) Nitrobenzene. (b) Anhydrous AlCl3.

questions.q: Write (a) the product of the addition of Br2 to ethene and (b) the colour change observed.
questions.answer: (a) 1,2-Dibromoethane. (b) The reddish-brown colour of bromine water is decolourised.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write the product obtained when ethyne reacts with cold alkaline KMnO4 and state the observation.
questions.answer: Ethyne is oxidised, first to a diketone and then to oxalic acid/sodium oxalate; the purple colour of KMnO4 disappears and brown MnO2 may separate.

questions.q: Describe the ozonolysis of ethene with equations.
questions.answer: CH2=CH2 + O3 → ozonide; ozonide + Zn/H2O → 2HCHO + ZnO (two molecules of methanal).

questions.q: What is pyrolysis (cracking) of alkanes? Give an example.
questions.answer: Heating alkanes at high temperature in the absence of air to break them into smaller hydrocarbons: C6H14 → C3H6 + C3H8 (also C2H4 + C4H10).

questions.q: State Markovnikov's rule with an example.
questions.answer: In the addition of an unsymmetrical reagent to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part adds to the carbon carrying fewer hydrogens. CH3CH=CH2 + HBr → CH3CHBrCH3.

questions.q: Why is benzene less reactive in addition but gives substitution reactions?
questions.answer: The delocalised π electron cloud gives great resonance stability (about 150 kJ mol^-1); addition would destroy aromaticity, whereas substitution retains it.

questions.q: Write the Wurtz reaction for the preparation of ethane.
questions.answer: 2CH3Br + 2Na → CH3–CH3 + 2NaBr (dry ether).

questions.q: What is the cause of the acidic nature of terminal alkynes? How is it shown?
questions.answer: The sp carbon is more electronegative (50% s character), making the C–H bond more polar; terminal alkynes give white (Ag) or red (Cu) precipitates with ammoniacal AgNO3 or Cu2Cl2.

questions.q: Distinguish between ethene and ethane by a chemical test.
questions.answer: Ethene decolourises bromine water (or Baeyer's reagent) while ethane does not.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of free-radical chlorination of methane.
questions.answer: Initiation: Cl2 → 2Cl• (UV). Propagation: Cl• + CH4 → HCl + •CH3; •CH3 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + Cl•. Termination: Cl• + Cl• → Cl2; •CH3 + •CH3 → C2H6; •CH3 + Cl• → CH3Cl.

questions.q: Explain the addition of HBr to propene with and without peroxide.
questions.answer: Without peroxide (Markovnikov): CH3CH=CH2 + HBr → CH3CHBrCH3 (2-bromopropane). With peroxide (anti-Markovnikov, free radical, Kharasch effect): CH3CH=CH2 + HBr → CH3CH2CH2Br (1-bromopropane).

questions.q: Write the structure and bonding of benzene and explain its aromatic character.
questions.answer: A planar hexagon of sp² carbons with six delocalised π electrons above and below the ring; all C–C bonds are equal (139 pm); resonance between two Kekulé structures; it follows Hückel's rule (4n + 2 = 6 π electrons), hence is aromatic and unusually stable.

questions.q: How will you convert (a) ethyne to benzene (b) ethene to ethanol (c) benzene to nitrobenzene?
questions.answer: (a) Passing ethyne through a red-hot iron tube (873 K) – trimerisation. (b) Hydration of ethene with water in the presence of H3PO4 or by H2SO4 followed by hydrolysis. (c) Treating benzene with a mixture of conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4 at 323–333 K.

questions.q: Explain the directive influence of –OH and –NO2 on electrophilic substitution of benzene.
questions.answer: –OH is electron-releasing by resonance (activating), so it directs the incoming group to ortho and para positions. –NO2 is electron-withdrawing (deactivating) and directs the incoming electrophile to the meta position.

questions.q: Distinguish between alkanes, alkenes and alkynes on the basis of hybridisation, shape and type of bond.
questions.answer: Alkanes: sp³, tetrahedral, only σ bonds; alkenes: sp², planar, one σ and one π; alkynes: sp, linear, one σ and two π bonds.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) How is ethene prepared in the laboratory? (b) Give the reactions of ethene with (i) HBr (ii) cold alkaline KMnO4 (iii) ozone followed by Zn/H2O. (c) Name the test used to distinguish alkenes from alkanes.
questions.answer:
(a) By heating ethanol with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K: CH3CH2OH → CH2=CH2 + H2O.
(b) (i) CH2=CH2 + HBr → CH3CH2Br. (ii) CH2=CH2 + [O] + H2O → HOCH2CH2OH (the purple colour disappears). (iii) CH2=CH2 + O3 → ozonide → 2HCHO.
(c) Bromine water or Baeyer's test (decolourisation).

questions.q: (a) Discuss the halogenation of alkanes: mechanism and reactivity. (b) Write the products of monochlorination of propane.
questions.answer:
(a) A free-radical chain reaction: initiation by sunlight forming Cl•; propagation by H abstraction and attack on Cl2; termination by radical coupling. The reactivity order of H is 3° > 2° > 1° and of halogens F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2.
(b) CH3CH2CH3 + Cl2 → CH3CH2CH2Cl (1-chloropropane) + CH3CHClCH3 (2-chloropropane) + HCl.

questions.q: (a) Describe the preparation of ethyne. (b) Explain its acidic character and give reactions with ammoniacal silver nitrate and water (HgSO4/H2SO4). (c) Write two uses.
questions.answer:
(a) CaC2 + 2H2O → HC≡CH + Ca(OH)2.
(b) The sp C–H bond is polar so the H is acidic: HC≡CH + 2[Ag(NH3)2]+ → AgC≡CAg (white) + ...; hydration: HC≡CH + H2O (HgSO4, H2SO4) → CH3CHO via the enol.
(c) Oxy-acetylene welding and manufacture of ethanal and PVC.

questions.q: (a) Explain the electrophilic substitution of benzene: nitration, halogenation, Friedel–Crafts alkylation and acylation. (b) Write the mechanism of nitration.
questions.answer:
(a) Nitration: C6H6 + HNO3 (H2SO4) → C6H5NO2. Halogenation: C6H6 + Cl2 (FeCl3) → C6H5Cl + HCl. Alkylation: C6H6 + CH3Cl (AlCl3) → C6H5CH3. Acylation: C6H6 + CH3COCl (AlCl3) → C6H5COCH3.
(b) HNO3 + 2H2SO4 → NO2+ + H3O+ + 2HSO4−; NO2+ attacks benzene to give the arenium ion, which loses H+ to restore aromaticity.
